deep.reconstruction:
Left column (main text). This is a draft of §5 of Riemann's Inauguraldissertation (1851), 'Grundlagen für eine allgemeine Theorie der Functionen einer veränderlichen complexen Grösse'. The published §5 opens with almost the same words: 'Für die folgenden Betrachtungen beschränken wir die Veränderlichkeit der Grössen x, y auf ein endliches Gebiet, indem wir als Ort des Punktes O nicht mehr die Ebene A selbst, sondern eine über dieselbe ausgebreitete Fläche T betrachten ... bei der es unanstössig sein wird, von auf einander liegenden Flächen zu reden.' The right-column insertions are revisions of this opening sentence.

Content, step by step:
(i) The variable point O = x+iy is restricted to a connected, bounded surface T spread over the plane A. Several sheets of T may lie over the same region of A.
(ii) Hypothesis: superposed sheets are never joined along a line. This excludes folds ('Umfaltung') and splitting along a line.
(iii) Draw any line l across the region covered by T. Away from the boundary of T, the number n of superposed sheets is the same on both sides. Give l a direction. Call the sheets on the left a_1..a_n and those on the right a'_1..a'_n. Each a_i continues across l into a definite a'_j. This assignment is locally constant along l, but it may change at an isolated point K of l.
(iv) Above K the rule is a_i -> a'_i; below K it is a_i -> a'_{alpha_i}, where alpha is a permutation of 1..n. A point circling K repeatedly therefore moves through sheets according to this permutation. Since the sheet set is finite and a_1 can only be re-entered from a_1's predecessor, the point returns to a_1 after m (≤ n) circuits; that is, it traverses the cycle of the permutation containing 1.
(v) K is common to these m sheets. On the next page it is called a 'Knotenpunkt (m-1)ter Ordnung', later 'Windungspunkt'. The remaining n-m sheets split likewise into cycles m_1, m_2, ... In modern terms this is the cycle decomposition of the local monodromy permutation at a branch point, and the ramification index of each cycle.

Right column (computation in pencil, not part of the dissertation text). Setting, inferred by me: Riemann appears to use parallel (geodesic normal) coordinates (s, p) near a boundary curve of curvature K. Here p is the normal distance and the area element is (1-Kp) dp ds. For a function lambda depending only on p, the Laplace equation becomes d/dp[(1-Kp) dlambda/dp] = 0.
(1) Integration gives (1-Kp) lambda' = const, so lambda' = a/(1-Kp).
(2) lambda = a log(1-Kp) + b. Strictly, lambda = -(a/K) log(1-Kp) + b; Riemann redefines or absorbs the constant. A crossed-out factor before 'a' suggests he first wrote it.
(3) Boundary values: lambda(p1) = gamma1 and lambda(p2) = gamma2. Hence gamma1 - gamma2 = a log[(1-Kp1)/(1-Kp2)], and a = (gamma1-gamma2)/L with L = log[(1-Kp1)/(1-Kp2)].
(4) Derivative: lambda' = (gamma1 - gamma2)/((1-Kp) L), with the constant K absorbed as above.
(5) Dirichlet integral over the strip: ∫∫ (lambda_p)^2 (1-Kp) dp ds. Per unit length this is (gamma1-gamma2)^2/L^2 ∫ dp/(1-Kp) (with the correct factor K^2 restored).
(6) Final result: ∫ (gamma1-gamma2)^2 K ds / [log(1-Kp1) - log(1-Kp2)].

Check on a circle: R = 1/K and 1-Kp = r/R. The result becomes 2π(gamma1-gamma2)^2/log(r1/r2), the classical Dirichlet energy (capacity) of an annulus.

The point of the computation is apparently the Dirichlet energy of the radial-type harmonic function in a thin strip along a curved boundary. The total-curvature integral ∫K ds appears, which ties in with the 'Gesammtkrümmung der Begrenzung' and the order-of-connectivity count on the following page.
errors: lambda = a log(1-Kp) + b is not the antiderivative of a/(1-Kp). The correct form is -(a/K) log(1-Kp) + b. It is harmless only if a is redefined, and the crossed-out factor suggests Riemann noticed this.

The line for dlambda/dp reads (as transcribed) 'gamma1 + gamma2'. Since a = (gamma1-gamma2)/L, it should be gamma1 - gamma2. It also lacks the factor -K under the original normalization of a. This is either a slip or a misreading.

The intermediate integral ∫(gamma1-gamma2)^2 dp / ((1-Kp)^2 L^2) omits the area weight (1-Kp). With the weight, the integrand is ∝ 1/(1-Kp). The final line K(gamma1-gamma2)^2/L is correct for the weighted integral with the factor K^2 restored, so the intermediate exponent is either a slip or the weight was understood implicitly.
In the text, the number of circuits should be m ≤ n (m = n is possible). A strict '<' would be wrong.

results.what: Surface T spread over the plane with superposed sheets not joined along lines; local monodromy permutation at an isolated point K; cycles of length m give a branch point of order m-1
results.modern_name: Riemann surface as a branched covering of the plane; ramification/branch points and cycle decomposition of local monodromy

results.what: Radial solution of d/dp((1-Kp) lambda') = 0 in parallel coordinates along a curve of curvature K, and its Dirichlet integral K(gamma1-gamma2)^2/log((1-Kp1)/(1-Kp2)) per unit length
results.modern_name: Dirichlet energy / condenser capacity of a thin curved strip (annulus capacity 2π/log(r2/r1) in the circular case)
results.usually_credited_to: classical potential theory (Green, Dirichlet, Gauss); annulus capacity is standard

deep.surprise_reason: The text is a known draft of §5 of Riemann's 1851 dissertation, introducing branch points via local monodromy, which is well known as his. The marginal computation is an elementary Dirichlet-integral calculation for a curved strip, standard potential theory. Its link to total boundary curvature and connectivity is a mildly interesting glimpse of how he may have approached the dissertation's curvature/connectivity argument, but it is not a new result.

checkable.asserts: Nonzero (= -a*K/(1-K*p) - a/(1-K*p)): Riemann's form a log(1-Kp)+b does not have derivative a/(1-Kp) without redefining a
With lambda = A log(1-Kp)+B, the boundary values gamma1, gamma2 give A = (g1-g2)/log((1-Kp1)/(1-Kp2)) (result 0)
Weighted Dirichlet integral per unit arc length equals K(g1-g2)^2/(log(1-Kp1)-log(1-Kp2)), Riemann's final line (result 0)
For a circle (K=1/R, total ∫K ds = 2π) the result reduces to the annulus energy 2π(g1-g2)^2/log(r1/r2) (result 0)

transcription_corrections: Right column top: 'indem wir als Ort des Punktes O nicht mehr die Ebene A selbst sondern eine über dieselbe ausgebreitete begrenzte Fläche T betrachten' and 'wobei es unanstössig sein wird, von auf einander liegenden Flächen zu reden' are insertions into the first sentence of §5 (cf. published text), not separate remarks.
In 'lambda = [-...-] a log(1-Kp)+b' the struck-out item looks like a constant factor (possibly 1/K or similar) written before 'a'.
'gamma1 + gamma2' in the dlambda/dp line is probably 'gamma1 - gamma2' (or a slip by Riemann).
The exponent of (1-Kp) in the dp-integral is unclear in the image (2 or possibly 4); the area-weighted integral requires net exponent 1.
'nach einer Anzahl von Umkreisungen die < als n ist': probably 'die ≤ n ist' / 'nicht > n'.
'Geben wir dieser Linie eine bestimmte Richtung bei-liebig[?]': read 'Geben wir dieser Linie eine bestimmte Richtung bei' (the 'liebig' fragment is doubtful).
